messages:
Evan: quick ask — onboarding mercury-7b into hosted catalog. Can someone run a lightweight smoke + batching sweep at 4k context? Need p50/p95 token latency, max steady tokens/s, and whether KV cache spill happens. No long profiling, just a fast pass we can publish to the model page.

Maya: I can take this. Do we want float16 baseline + q4_0 sweep? Also which batch sizes to try?

Evan: baseline fp16 + q4_0 + q2_k for comparison. Try batch sizes [1,2,4,8] for single-request latency and [16,32,64] for throughput mix. Target GPU: g5.2xlarge equivalent (A100-ish).

Juan: tagging in bench-bot for an automated run. bench-bot, please start smoke sweep: mercury-7b, seq=4096, batches as above, quant=[fp16,q4_0,q2_k], warmup=50, measure=500 tokens.

bench-bot: acknowledged — queued run #4251. ETA ~8m. (run id: rb-4251)

Sasha: FYI if you hit long p95s at batch 1 it's usually KV cache misses; try enabling prefix caching in the runner: `--kv-cache true`. Also consider `--cuda-graphs on` for the fp16 path to reduce jitter.

Maya: noted. I'll run two passes: with and without cuda graphs. Will post condensed table here.

bench-bot: run #4251 complete. Summary (seq=4096, warmup=50, measure=500):
- fp16, batch=1 -> p50=18ms/token, p95=42ms/token, steady=320 tok/s
- fp16, batch=8 -> p50=6ms/token, p95=14ms/token, steady=1500 tok/s
- q4_0, batch=1 -> p50=14ms/token, p95=36ms/token, steady=380 tok/s
- q4_0, batch=8 -> p50=4.5ms/token, p95=12ms/token, steady=1700 tok/s
- q2_k, batch=1 -> p50=16ms/token, p95=40ms/token, steady=350 tok/s
- q2_k, batch=8 -> p50=5.2ms/token, p95=13.5ms/token, steady=1600 tok/s
(note: cuda-graphs disabled for this run)

Evan: nice. Can you also run a quick KV-cache-enabled pass for fp16 batch=1 to check p95 delta? That's the main customer-facing latency.

Maya: requeued run #4252 (fp16, batch=1, kv-cache=true, cuda-graphs=on).

bench-bot: run #4252 complete. fp16 batch=1 kv-cache=true cuda-graphs=on -> p50=12ms/token, p95=22ms/token, steady=420 tok/s.

Juan: that's a solid improvement on p95. Do we have memory footprint numbers (GPU memory) for these quant modes at seq=4096? Might affect Dedicated packing.

bench-bot: approximate GPU memory (inclusive overhead): fp16 ~24.8GB, q4_0 ~17.6GB, q2_k ~13.9GB. (measured during steady state)

Sasha: thanks — those numbers suggest q4_0 is the best sweet spot for cost vs latency here. For rollout I'd recommend defaulting to q4_0 with fp16 fallback if we detect quality/regression. Add an automatic fallback route that triggers when token lat > 30ms p95 for batch<=1.

Priya: can someone paste the runner command you used? I'll add it to the onboarding doc.

Maya: command I ran:```bash
run-bench --model mercury-7b --seq 4096 --quant fp16 --batch 1 --warmup 50 --measure 500 --kv-cache true --cuda-graphs on --gpu-type g5x
run-bench --model mercury-7b --seq 4096 --quant q4_0 --batch 8 --warmup 50 --measure 500 --kv-cache false --cuda-graphs off --gpu-type g5x
```

Evan: perfect. Maya — can you drop the summarized table + the run id links into the PR for model-catalog (PR: #312) so docs/ops can reference? Also note the kv-cache and memory numbers.

Maya: will do in ~15m. Also adding a short note: observed occasional tail spike at 1/500 samples for q4_0 batch=8 (p99 ~28ms/token). Logging link: https://benching.internal/runs/rb-4251

Juan: fine to merge once Maya posts the PR update. After that we can spin a short canary to internal beta.

Evan: thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) publish q4_0 as preferred for hosted launch, (2) add fp16 fallback route, (3) ops to validate Dedicated packing using mem numbers. I'll write the rollout ticket after PR merge. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: archived run outputs to /var/bench/mercury7b/rb-4251 and /var/bench/mercury7b/rb-4252.
